# google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy

A PscAuthorizationPolicy represents an instance-level policy specified by a producer for control over destination connectivity via PSC.


To get more information about PscAuthorizationPolicy, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/reference/networkconnectivity/rest/v1/projects.locations.pscAuthorizationPolicies)
* How-to Guides
    * [About Service Connectivity Automation](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/about-service-connectivity-automation)


## Example Usage - Network Connectivity Psc Authorization Policy Basic


```hcl
resource "google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy" "default" {
  psc_authorization_policy_id = "my-psc-auth-policy"
  location                    = "us-central1"
  target_resource_uri         = "//agentregistry.googleapis.com/projects/my-project-name/locations/global"
  authorized_client_resources = ["*"]
  authorization_mode          = "AUTHORIZATION_MODE_TRANSITIVE_TO_SERVICE_ATTACHMENT"
}
```

## Example Usage - Network Connectivity Psc Authorization Policy Full


```hcl
resource "google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy" "default" {
  psc_authorization_policy_id = "my-psc-auth-policy-full"
  location                    = "us-east1"
  description                 = "My PscAuthorizationPolicy"
  target_resource_uri         = "//agentregistry.googleapis.com/projects/my-project-name/locations/global"
  authorized_client_resources = ["projects/my-project-name"]
  authorization_mode          = "AUTHORIZATION_MODE_TRANSITIVE_TO_SERVICE_ATTACHMENT"

  labels = {
    env = "default"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `authorization_mode` -
  (Required)
  The authorization mode of the PscAuthorizationPolicy.
  Possible values:
  AUTHORIZATION_MODE_TRANSITIVE_TO_SERVICE_ATTACHMENT

* `authorized_client_resources` -
  (Required)
  The list of authorized consumer resources that are allowed to
  connect to the target resource. The list is limited to 1 value, and can be
  one of the following:
  * `projects/{project_id}`: A specific project ID.
  * `*`: Wildcard to allow any consumer.

* `target_resource_uri` -
  (Required)
  The full, absolute URI of the targeted resource governed by this
  policy. Format:
  `//agentregistry.googleapis.com/projects/{project}/locations/{location}`

* `location` -
  (Required)
  Resource ID segment making up resource `name`. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.

* `psc_authorization_policy_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID to use for the PscAuthorizationPolicy, which will become the final component of the PscAuthorizationPolicy's resource name.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  A description of this resource.

* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  User-defined labels.
  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

## Import


PscAuthorizationPolicy can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/pscAuthorizationPolicies/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import PscAuthorizationPolicy using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    location = "<-required value->"
    pscAuthorizationPolicyId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import PscAuthorizationPolicy using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/pscAuthorizationPolicies/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}"
  to = google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), PscAuthorizationPolicy can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/pscAuthorizationPolicies/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_psc_authorization_policy.default {{location}}/{{psc_authorization_policy_id}}
```
